Who we are

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

About the role:

This is a high energy role in which you will bring the Internet of Things to small to medium size customers, building Samsara's business and bringing the benefits of sensor data to customers. Typical sales will be $5k to $20k, and typically involve proof of concepts, multiple stakeholders, multi-faceted pricing negotiations, and selling to owners, safety and operational managers.

This position is based remotely in Canada.

You should apply if:

  • You want to impact the industries that run our world: Your efforts will result in real-world impact—helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely.
  • Your mantra is #alwaysbeprospecting: The world of operations is vast. Your customers are often out in the field and the best way to catch them is live on the phone. Samsara’s top reps do constant research to find companies and contacts to expand their pipeline.
  • You have innate curiosity in how businesses work: One day you’ll meet with someone in waste management and the next you may be learning about the inner workings of a food distribution center. Our top sales team members seek to learn the ins and outs of the businesses they support in order to make a larger impact.
  • You are a life-long learner: Samsara sales are complex. You will need to learn about businesses where you previously had little knowledge. The payoff is big but you have to be willing to put in the work.
  • You build genuine relationships with your customers: The industries we serve have relied on pen-and-paper solutions for years and haven’t been met with the type of technology we offer. Our customers value earned trust and human relationships built over time.
  • You want to be with the best: Samsara’s high-performance Sales culture means you’ll be surrounded by the best and challenged to go farther than you have before.

In this role, you will:

  • Own customer engagements end-to-end, from prospecting and qualification to close.
  • Generate pipeline through strategic outbound prospecting, as well as receive inbound leads from our account development team.
  • Target accounts with 11-30 vehicles.
  • Experience handling and owning transactional sales process with high volume demands.
  • Champion, role model, and embed Samsara’s cultural principles (Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team) as we scale globally and across new offices.

Minimum requirements for this role:

  • 1+ years of experience in a closing sales role

An ideal candidate has:

  • Proven track record of consistent quota achievement
  • Experience selling in the commercial space - small to medium deals sizes
  • Experience with high-volume cold calling
  • Experience in fast-paced, transactional sales
  • Must demonstrate a growth mindset and a willingness to be collaborative with your teammates and in your selling process
  • SFDC familiarity

$140,500—$154,550 CAD

Total Rewards

At Samsara, we build for the people who keep the global economy moving. We want owners, not passengers, which is why our rewards are designed to fuel high-impact builders. Our compensation program delivers above-market total compensation through a combination of base salary, performance-based bonus/variable pay, and equity (for eligible roles) in a high-growth public company. We meaningfully differentiate pay for our top performers, who have the opportunity to earn above-market compensation that can outpace the broader market over time.

Beyond compensation, we provide the foundations that enable long-term success: a flexible, employee-led remote model, a professional development stipend, comprehensive health and parental leave plans, and more. If you’re ready to build for the long term and own the outcome, your journey starts here.

Flexible Working

At Samsara, we embrace a flexible working model that caters to the diverse needs of our teams. Our offices are open for those who prefer to work in-person and we also support remote work where it aligns with our operational requirements. For certain positions, being close to one of our offices or within a specific geographic area is important to facilitate collaboration, access to resources, or alignment with our service regions. In these cases, the job description will clearly indicate any working location requirements. Our goal is to ensure that all members of our team can contribute effectively, whether they are working on-site, in a hybrid model, or fully remotely. jobs.description:
Job Title: Invoice Processing Specialist

Job Type: (Remote)

Job Summary

The Invoice Processing Specialist — Accounts Receivable is responsible for preparing, reviewing, processing, and maintaining customer invoices and accounts receivable transactions. This position ensures invoices are accurate, timely, properly recorded, and aligned with customer contracts, sales orders, pricing agreements, and company policies.

The role also supports customer account reconciliation, payment application, collections coordination, and resolution of billing discrepancies to help maintain accurate accounts receivable records and healthy cash flow.

Key Responsibilities

  • Prepare and process customer invoices accurately and within established billing schedules.

  • Review sales orders, contracts, purchase orders, service agreements, and supporting documentation before invoicing.

  • Verify customer information, billing addresses, pricing, quantities, tax codes, payment terms, and discounts.

  • Enter and maintain invoices in the accounting or ERP system.

  • Generate recurring, milestone, project-based, and other customer invoices as required.

  • Process credit memos, debit memos, adjustments, and billing corrections.

  • Ensure invoices comply with customer requirements and contractual billing terms.

  • Review invoices for accuracy and completeness before distribution to customers.

  • Distribute invoices through email, electronic billing portals, EDI, or other approved methods.

  • Monitor invoice status and follow up on rejected, disputed, or returned invoices.

  • Research and resolve billing discrepancies in collaboration with Sales, Customer Service, Operations, and Finance teams.

  • Maintain accurate customer account and billing records.

  • Apply customer payments to the appropriate invoices and accounts when required.

  • Reconcile customer accounts and investigate unapplied or unidentified payments.

  • Assist with accounts receivable aging analysis and identify overdue customer balances.

  • Coordinate with collections personnel regarding past-due invoices and customer disputes.

  • Respond to customer inquiries regarding invoices, account balances, payment status, and billing documentation.

  • Prepare customer statements and account summaries.

  • Assist with month-end and year-end accounts receivable closing activities.

  • Reconcile accounts receivable subledger balances to the general ledger.

Job Description

This is a full-time remote position that can be located anywhere in the U.S

We are hiring a Senior Information Systems Engineer to build and support engineering and automation of our End User Computing (EUC) platform. You will manage Windows endpoints through Microsoft Intune, deliver virtual desktops on Amazon Workspaces, and automate the work end to end with scripting, the Microsoft Graph API and Ansible.

This is a hands-on senior role. You will resolve escalated L2/L3 issues, replace manual processes with code, and mentor L1 support staff.

Key responsibilities

Endpoint management (Microsoft Intune)

  • Design, build and maintain Intune configuration profiles, compliance policies, app deployments and update rings for Windows devices.
  • Automate device, app and policy management through the Microsoft Graph API, including bulk changes, reporting and audit exports.
  • Manage Windows Autopilot enrolment and zero-touch provisioning for new and refreshed devices.
  • Integrate Intune with Entra ID (Azure AD) Conditional Access, groups and identity lifecycle processes.

Virtual desktops (Amazon Workspaces)

  • Build and maintain Amazon Workspaces bundles, custom images and directory integration.
  • Automate Workspaces provisioning, patching, rebuilding and decommissioning through the AWS CLI, SDKs or APIs.
  • Monitor Workspaces performance, cost and utilization, and right-size running modes and bundles.
  • Apply AWS security controls such as IAM, security groups, IP access control groups and encryption.

Automation and configuration management

  • Write and maintain scripts in PowerShell, Python and Bash to automate repeatable EUC tasks.
  • Develop Ansible playbooks and roles for endpoint and virtual desktop configuration, patching and compliance.
  • Store code in Git, follow peer review, and run automation through CI/CD pipelines where suitable.

Operations and support

  • Act as the L2/L3 escalation point for complex endpoint, application and virtual desktop incidents.
  • Run root-cause analysis on recurring issues and deliver permanent fixes.
  • Produce and maintain technical documentation, runbooks and knowledge base articles.
  • Mentor L1 engineers and service desk staff and contribute to EUC standards and roadmap.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems or a related field, or equivalent experience.
  • 5+ years in IT systems engineering, with at least 3 years focused on End User Computing.
  • Scripting: strong PowerShell skills, plus working knowledge of Python and/or Bash for automation and API integration.
  • Microsoft Intune with API: hands-on Intune administration at scale, and proven automation through the Microsoft Graph API (authentication via app registrations, REST calls, paging and throttling).
  • Ansible Nice to have: experience writing playbooks, roles and inventories to manage Windows
  • Amazon Workspaces: experience deploying and operating Workspaces, including bundles, custom images, directory services and lifecycle automation.
  • Solid grounding in Windows 10/11 and Entra ID / Active Directory, Group Policy and core networking (DNS, DHCP, VPN).
  • Experience with Git version control and ITSM tools such as ServiceNow or Jira Service Management.

Preferred qualifications

  • Infrastructure-as-code experience with Terraform or AWS CloudFormation.
  • Exposure to other VDI/DaaS platforms such as Azure Virtual Desktop, Windows 365 or Citrix.
  • Experience with Microsoft Defender for Endpoint and endpoint security baselines (CIS, Microsoft Security Baselines).
  • Packaging experience with Win32 apps, MSIX or PSAppDeployToolkit.
  • Relevant certifications, for example: Microsoft Certified: Endpoint Administrator Associate (MD-102), AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Associate or SysOps Administrator – Associate, and Red Hat Certified Specialist in Ansible Automation (Nice to Have)

Skills and attributes

  • An automation-first mindset: you script a task the second time you do it.
  • Clear written and verbal communication with technical and non-technical users.
  • Structured troubleshooting and calm ownership of high-impact incidents.
  • Comfortable working independently and setting technical direction for a small team.

Benefits

We’re committed to supporting your ultimate well-being through our total compensation package offerings that support your health, wealth and self. These offerings include Medical, Dental, Vision, Health Savings Accounts / Flexible Spending Accounts, Life and AD&D Insurance, 401(k), Tuition Reimbursement, and an array of resources that encourage a lifetime of healthier living. Benefits eligibility may differ depending on full-time or part-time status. Compensation depends on the applicable US geographic market. The expected base pay for this position ranges from $91,000 - $110,000 annually, and will be based on a number of additional factors including skills, experience, and education.

The Company is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, religion, color, national origin, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, status as a protected veteran, among other things, or status as a qualified individual with disability.

Employee Relations & Compliance (Primary Focus)

Program & Process Support

Qualifications

jobs.description:
Selection process developed by matteria

Location and Work Mode

Remote role based in Argentina or Mexico.

Who we are

The Nature Conservancy (TNC) is a global environmental nonprofit working to create a world where people and nature thrive. Founded in 1951, TNC advances conservation with the support of more than a million members and the work of over 400 scientists, impacting conservation in +80 countries and territories.

Our impact

Since its founding in 1951, The Nature Conservancy has grown to become one of the most effective and wide-reaching environmental organizations in the world. Some key accomplishments include:

  • 80+ countries and territories where TNC impacts conservation.

  • 125M+ acres of land protected.

  • 400+ scientists on staff.

  • 1M+ members supporting our mission.

Purpose of the Position

The Senior Donor Communications Officer translates TNC's conservation priorities, results, and funding needs into compelling, donor-centered communications that support fundraising across Latin America.

As a strategic partner to the Director of Donor Communications, the role leads complex, multi-country initiatives and strengthens the quality, consistency, and persuasive power of communications for major and principal gift audiences. It is a senior individual contributor role, reporting to the Director of Donor Communications.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic planning and advisory

  • Partner with the Director of Donor Communications to develop regional communications strategies, priorities, messaging frameworks, and content plans aligned with fundraising and conservation objectives.

  • Advise Development colleagues, conservation teams, and regional leaders on donor positioning, narrative strategy, audience needs, and communications opportunities.

  • Exercise independent judgment to resolve complex messaging challenges, reconcile competing stakeholder inputs, and maintain donor relevance, accuracy, and strategic alignment.

  • Represent Donor Communications in designated regional, global, and cross-functional initiatives, meetings, and planning processes.

  • Provide continuity and senior-level decision support to the Director within agreed responsibilities.

Donor communications and persuasive storytelling

  • Lead high-priority communications for donor cultivation, solicitation, stewardship, campaigns, and major or principal gift opportunities.

  • Develop or oversee funding proposals, concept notes, regional and country overviews, donor visit materials, stewardship reports, campaign collateral, presentations, impact reports, and leadership messages.

  • Translate complex conservation, financial, and programmatic information into accurate, engaging narratives that inspire philanthropic support.

  • Adapt messaging to donor interests, cultural contexts, audience needs, and stages of the fundraising relationship.

  • Ensure communications do more than report information: they must explain why the work matters and why donors should support it.

Project and stakeholder leadership

  • Lead complex communications initiatives from initial briefing and strategy through stakeholder alignment, execution, review, delivery, and evaluation.

  • Define objectives, audiences, deliverables, timelines, responsibilities, risks, and trade-offs.

  • Coordinate contributors across countries, functions, and seniority levels in a matrixed environment.

  • Influence without relying on formal authority, facilitate decisions, and maintain momentum when priorities compete.

  • Take ownership of outcomes end to end rather than limiting responsibility to an individual writing assignment.

Functional leadership and capability building

  • Strengthen editorial standards, regional messaging consistency, multilingual content practices, and donor communications workflows.

  • Provide mentorship, constructive feedback, and subject-matter guidance to communications and Development colleagues.

  • Identify opportunities to improve the quality, effectiveness, and efficiency of content production, tools, systems, and processes.

  • Oversee relevant vendor relationships and support training and knowledge-sharing across the region.

  • Promote effective use of digital collaboration tools and AI-assisted content solutions while maintaining accuracy and institutional standards.

Multilingual and cross-cultural collaboration

  • Develop and review content in English, Spanish, and Portuguese according to audience and business needs.

  • Collaborate directly with colleagues in Brazil and other Latin American markets, including in conversations where English may not be the primary working language.

  • Navigate cultural and organizational differences to build trust, ensure local relevance, and facilitate alignment across regional and global teams.

Requirements and competencies to work with us

Education

  • Bachelor's degree in Communications, Journalism, Marketing, Philanthropy, International Affairs, Conservation, or a related field.

  • An equivalent combination of education and relevant professional experience may be considered.

Experience

  • At least 5 to 7 years of relevant experience in donor communications, fundraising communications, strategic communications, or a related field.

  • Demonstrated experience developing audience-focused communications that support fundraising, persuasion, engagement, campaigns, or other organizational objectives.

  • Experience leading complex cross-functional, regional, or multi-country projects from planning through delivery.

  • Experience advising senior stakeholders, influencing without direct authority, and aligning competing priorities.

  • Experience producing a range of communication formats, including proposals, presentations, reports, campaign materials, and strategic narratives.

Knowledge and Skills

  • Strategic communications planning and narrative development.

  • Fundraising communications, donor engagement, and persuasive writing.

  • Strong writing, editing, synthesis, and storytelling skills.

  • Ability to interpret scientific, conservation, financial, and programmatic information.

  • Project management, prioritization, and delivery across multiple workstreams.

  • Stakeholder management and facilitation in matrixed organizations.

  • Editorial quality assurance and multilingual content coordination.

  • Desirable: familiarity with content management systems, project management platforms, digital storytelling, and AI-assisted content tools.

Languages

  • English: Professional fluency, with very strong writing, editing, and verbal communication skills.

  • Spanish: Professional fluency, with very strong writing, editing, and verbal communication skills.

  • Portuguese: Advanced working proficiency sufficient to understand discussions, participate in meetings, and collaborate directly with Portuguese-speaking colleagues, particularly in Brazil.

Competencies

  • Strategic thinking: Understands the organizational and fundraising context behind each communication.

  • Donor-centered storytelling: Connects the work being done with donor motivations, interests, and potential contributions.

  • Ownership and proactivity: Anticipates needs, identifies opportunities, and drives work forward with autonomy.

  • Influence and collaboration: Builds alignment across cultures, functions, and seniority levels.

  • Adaptability and sound judgment: Manages ambiguity, competing priorities, sensitive information, and complex stakeholder dynamics.

Our team profile

The successful candidate will join an experienced, collaborative, and relatively horizontal team that values initiative, expertise, and constructive partnership over formal hierarchy. They should be comfortable operating as a senior contributor who can influence peers and support the team without relying on direct managerial authority. The team is looking for someone who:

  • Is curious about the work behind the message. Invests time in understanding conservation projects, funding needs, and organizational priorities rather than simply receiving a brief and producing copy.

  • Takes initiative. Anticipates needs, identifies opportunities, and contributes beyond narrowly defined assignments when the broader objective requires it.

  • Combines autonomy with collaboration. Owns deliverables end to end while involving the right stakeholders and respecting colleagues' expertise.

  • Navigates complexity diplomatically. Reconciles different perspectives, works across geographies, and builds trust without relying on authority.

  • Values quality and impact. Understands that communications must be accurate, engaging, and useful to the fundraising process, not simply well written.

Key interests for working with us

The team seeks someone motivated by the opportunity to connect philanthropic resources with meaningful environmental and social outcomes.

Relevant interests include:

  • Biodiversity conservation and ecosystem protection.

  • Climate change mitigation and adaptation.

  • Protection of land, oceans, freshwater, forests, and other critical natural systems.

  • Sustainable food and water systems.

  • The relationship between nature, community wellbeing, and long-term resilience.

  • The role of philanthropy and strategic partnerships in enabling conservation at scale.

Reasons to join our team

  • Mission-driven work: Contribute to a global organization working to conserve nature and address interconnected environmental challenges.

  • Regional reach: Support fundraising and conservation initiatives across diverse Latin American countries and cultural contexts.

  • Strategic influence: Help shape the narratives and communications practices that support major and principal gift fundraising.

  • Professional autonomy: Lead complex initiatives and exercise independent judgment in a senior individual contributor role.

  • Multidisciplinary collaboration: Work closely with Development, conservation, communications, and regional leadership colleagues.

  • Remote work: Work remotely from an approved location in Argentina or Mexico.

Relevant details before applying for this vacancy

  • Role scope: This is a senior strategic communications position with substantial hands-on writing and editing responsibilities. It is not exclusively a strategy or management role.

  • Sector flexibility: Candidates from agencies, corporate communications, campaigns, public relations, marketing, and other persuasive communications environments may be considered, even without prior environmental nonprofit experience.

  • TNC is an Equal Opportunity Employer and offers accommodations in the application process for qualified individuals with disabilities.

Job Title: Senior Advisor, Regulatory Starting Material

Job Location: Remote, Indiana, United States of America

At Lilly, the work is demanding because patients are waiting. We unite caring with discovery to help make life better for people around the world, knowing that every decision, every detail, and every day matters. Headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana, our over 50,000 employees around the globe take on complex challenges to discover and deliver life-changing medicines, strengthen how health is understood and managed, and support the communities we serve. This is hard, urgent, selfless work—but it’s work worth doing. If you’re driven by purpose and ready to bring your best to work that truly matters for patients, we invite you to join us.


Overview:

Centessa Pharmaceuticals, a wholly owned subsidiary of Eli Lilly and Company, is a clinical-stage company developing orexin receptor 2 (OX2R) agonists as a new class of medicines for the treatment of narcolepsy and potentially other sleep-wake disorders. Centessa’s lead investigational candidate – cleminorexton (formerly ORX750) – is being developed for narcolepsy type 1, narcolepsy type 2, and idiopathic hypersomnia. Centessa's OX2R agonist portfolio includes additional clinical and preclinical-stage assets with potential utility across a broader range of neurological, neurodegenerative, and neuropsychiatric conditions.Headquartered in Boston, Massachusetts, Centessa was recognized as a Great Place to Work® in 2026.

Position Summary:

Centessa iscurrently seeking a Senior Advisor, Regulatory Starting Material. The individual in this Associate Director level role will lead the strategy, justification, and regulatory positioning of Regulatory Starting Materials for drug substance manufacturing processes supporting late-stage clinical and commercial programs.Reporting to the Vice President, CMC, this role will serve as the internal and external subject matter expert on RSM selection in accordance with ICH Q11 and applicable regional guidance, ensuring synthetic routes, GMP starting points, and supply strategies are scientifically sound, regulatorily defensible, and aligned with commercial manufacturing readiness. This individual will partner closely with Process Chemistry, Analytical Development, Regulatory Affairs, Quality, and external manufacturing partners to build and defend RSM strategy through health authority interactions and regulatory submissions.

Responsibilities:

  • Lead the identification, justification, and regulatory strategy for Regulatory Starting Materials across drug substance synthetic routes, in accordance with ICH Q11 and relevant regional guidance/reflection papers.

  • Actively manage the starting material resupply campaigns and scale-up efforts, including on-going inventory, production forecast, manufacturing timing, production suite slot reservations, and contracting.

  • Author and review CMC regulatory submission content related to RSM selection and justification (e.g., Module 3 sections, briefing documents, agency responses) in support of INDs/NDAs /MAAs.

  • Prepare and lead health authority interactions (e.g., Type C meetings, scientific advice procedures) related to starting material strategy; develop briefing packages and represent the company in agency discussions.

  • Partner with Process Chemistry and Analytical Development to evaluate synthetic routes, assess structural relevance of candidate starting materials, and support impurity fate-and-purge and risk assessments that inform RSM designation.

  • Define and document the boundary between non-GMP and GMP manufacturing steps for drug substance processes, ensuring alignment with CMOs and internal quality standards.

  • Lead technology transfer and process changes affecting RSM designation as programs advance from late-stage clinical development toward commercial manufacturing.

  • Manage relationships with drug substance/API CMOs and RSM suppliers, including technical oversight, site visits, and support for supplier qualification and dual-sourcing strategies.

  • Monitor evolving global regulatory guidance and agency precedent on starting material selection; translate changes into updated internal strategy, templates, and risk assessments.

  • Collaborate cross-functionally with Regulatory Affairs, Quality, Supply Chain, and Manufacturing to ensure RSM strategy supports program timelines, submission readiness, and commercial supply continuity.

  • Support due diligence activities (e.g., licensing, partnering) requiring assessment of drug substance manufacturing routes and starting material risk.

  • Provide subject matter expertise during regulatory inspections and audits related to drug substance manufacturing and starting material justification.

  • Build, lead, and mentor a team supporting RSM and drug substance CMC strategy activities (scope dependent on level).

  • Domestic and international travel required (approximately 10–20%).

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Advanced degree in chemistry, chemical engineering, or a related field; PhD strongly preferred.

  • 7+ years of relevant experience in CMC, process chemistry or drug substance/API development and manufacturing, including demonstrated leadership of starting material or CMC regulatory strategy programs.

  • Demonstrated experience supporting late-stage clinical and/or commercial drug substance programs.

  • Deep working knowledge of ICH Q11 and applicable regional guidance/expectations governing the selection and justification of Regulatory Starting Materials.

  • Demonstrated experience authoring and defending CMC regulatory submission content, including direct experience in health authority interactions related to starting material or drug substance manufacturing strategy.

  • Strong background in synthetic/process chemistry, with the ability to critically evaluate route scouting, impurity control strategy, and structural relevance arguments for candidate starting materials.

  • Experience managing relationships with drug substance/API CMOs and raw material suppliers, including batch record reviews and overarching manufacturing oversight.

  • Working knowledge of cGMP requirements as they apply to drug substance manufacturing and the GMP/non-GMP boundary.

  • Experience supporting technology transfer of drug substance processes from clinical to commercial scale preferred.

  • Strong leadership, cross-functional collaboration, and scientific writing/communication skills; exercises judgment within broadly defined practices and policies in determining solutions and actions.

  • Demonstrated ability to identify and address starting material-related risks that could jeopardize regulatory timelines, supply, or overall program success.

  • Use the Kite works encrypted email system for correspondence with patients and providers

  • Develop an organized, concise, and compliant way to manage assigned patient cases within established time frames

Compliance, Safety Reporting, and Communication

  • Operate within the tighter content controls and system permissions that apply to this role

  • Link the patient access support to meet patient needs, using Brand RC-approved materials
  • Conduct yourself with the utmost discretion and confidentiality
  • Adhere to strict company compliance guidelines and procedures
  • Work and lead cross-functionally with internal and external colleagues, compliantly, to improve the patient access journey
  • Effectively link customer insights to the offerings and approved resources to address patient access barriers

Period of Performance: January 1, 2027 through December 31, 2031, if all four option periods are exercised.

Summary of Services

The Inpatient/Outpatient Coder will remotely review VA health records and accurately code inpatient episodes and outpatient encounters for VISN 7. The role includes assigning and validating diagnosis and procedure codes, completing required data entry, resolving coding questions, and maintaining required accuracy and turnaround standards.

Mandatory Qualifications

Must be a U.S. citizen and be able to read, write, speak, and understand English.

Must have at least two years of coding experience in the specific coding area assigned.

Must have formal training in anatomy and physiology, medical terminology, pathology and disease processes, pharmacology, health-record content, reimbursement methodologies, and current coding systems.

Ensures the integrity, security, availability, reliability, and performance of network infrastructure by leveraging modern, software-defined approaches, including network programmability and Infrastructure as Code practices.

The Lead Network Engineer leads the planning, installation, monitoring, and automated management of complex network systems, delivering top-tier technical support to internal clients. Evaluates, tests, and recommends new network technologies, with a strategic focus on automation and cloud networking, to continuously improve efficiency and align with enterprise modernization objectives.

This role is accountable for complying with all applicable laws and regulations as well as internal policies and standards associated with assigned duties and responsibilities.

How You Contribute to the Company’s Mission in this Role:

Technical Architecture and Modernization

  • Leads the planning, design, testing, and automated deployment of network architectures across multiple platforms, including data center, WAN, campus, and cloud environments. Ensures all network solutions, including hardware and software, meet enterprise standards for security, availability, reliability, and performance.

  • Continuously evaluates new technologies, including SDN controllers, cloud networking services, and advanced automation tools, and drives modernization to support cloud adoption and business needs.

Network Automation and Software-Defined Operations

  • Champions and implements network automation and orchestration capabilities as a core function of the network team. Develops and maintains automation frameworks, including automated provisioning scripts, configuration templating systems, and version-controlled network configurations, to streamline routine network changes and reduce manual effort.

  • Integrates network management with DevOps practices using CI/CD pipelines for infrastructure updates and policy deployment to ensure consistency and agility in network operations.

  • Guides the transition toward software-defined networking and APIs for network programmability, ensuring the network can be managed as code for rapid scaling and improved reliability.

Strategic and Tactical Planning

  • Develops and recommends network strategies that align with broader IT and business goals. Actively participates in technology roadmaps and cross-functional planning to enable digital transformation initiatives, including cloud migration and SDN implementations.

  • Evaluates and selects new network solutions, including automation platforms, across on-premise and cloud platforms to ensure the organization adopts the most effective, scalable, and cost-efficient technology options.

Team Leadership and Knowledge Sharing

  • Provides technical leadership and mentorship in network automation and best practices to peers and junior engineers. Promotes a culture of continuous improvement by encouraging innovation in process automation, network monitoring, and self-healing networks.

  • Leads by example in using both traditional networking expertise and software development skills to solve complex problems. Frequently presents and transfers knowledge on new networking trends, including cloud, SDN, and AI/ML in networking, to the team, fostering professional growth and readiness for future network initiatives.

Business Alignment and Collaboration

  • Builds strong relationships with business stakeholders to understand requirements, pain points, and objectives. Ensures that network solutions, including automation efforts, directly support critical business needs such as improving operational efficiency, reliability, and security in alignment with enterprise IT strategy.

  • Collaborates with cross-functional teams, including Security, Cloud, and Application teams, to integrate networking seamlessly into broader infrastructure and cloud projects.

Compliance and Standardization

  • Ensures that all network changes and architectures adhere to corporate security policies, regulatory requirements, and industry best practices. Implements standardized processes, including change management and governance for network automation tools, to maintain compliance and auditability of network configurations.

  • Performs other job-related duties as assigned, within scope of responsibilities.

Required Qualifications

Education

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science or related field is required.

  • Four years of relevant work experience may be substituted for a bachelor’s degree.

  • Industry certifications approved by management, such as Cisco CCNA or Cisco DevNet Associate, may be considered in lieu of some years of experience.

Work Experience

  • Minimum of seven years of progressive network engineering experience in a large-scale, complex environment required.

  • Extensive background in enterprise network systems and programming required, including significant hands-on expertise in multiple of the following key domains:

  • Network Automation and Scripting:Proficiency in Python programming and/or other scripting languages for network automation, including use of RESTful APIs, Ansible, and Netmiko. Experience implementing Infrastructure as Code, including Terraform, to define and manage network infrastructure via automated pipelines is highly desired.

  • CI/CD and Orchestration:

  • Experience designing or using CI/CD and GitOps workflows for network configuration management and automated deployment processes to ensure consistent, repeatable changes across network environments.

  • Software-Defined Networking:n-depth knowledge of software-defined network architectures, such as Cisco ACI, VMware NSX, SD-WAN solutions, and multi-cloud networking across Azure and AWS environments. Familiarity with modern network programmability frameworks, including controller-driven and API-centric networking, and policy-driven network segmentation technologies.

  • Traditional Network Infrastructure:Strong background in core route/switch protocols, including BGP and OSPF, firewall administration, including Palo Alto and Cisco ASA, load balancers, network access control, including Cisco ISE, wireless networks, and network performance monitoring tools.

  • Multi-Platform and Hybrid Infrastructure:Experience designing and supporting network connectivity across on-premise data centers and cloud platforms, including Azure. Familiarity with virtualization and container networking, including VMware, Hyper-V, Kubernetes, and cloud VPC/VNet design, is preferred.

Other Technical Skills:

  • Demonstrated deep technical knowledge across a broad range of IT disciplines at an architectural level. Capable of analyzing and solving complex network problems, with strong troubleshooting skills and experience using advanced diagnostics, simulation tools, and network analytics.

Skills and Abilities

  • Strong communication skills and business acumen, with the ability to translate complex network concepts into business terms and negotiate solutions across multiple departments.

  • Recognized technical leader who proactively recommends process improvements for the network technology stack and stays current with industry advancements, including cloud networking, automation, and security.

  • Regularly meets with peers and vendors to resolve complex network issues, analyzes business requirements, and weighs alternatives to recommend optimal, cost-effective solutions.

  • Contributes significantly to network strategy and architecture decisions and advises senior management on emerging network technologies and approaches.

  • Demonstrates creativity and strong analytical ability in solving difficult problems and developing innovative approaches to meet objectives.

  • Ability to provide technical leadership, mentorship, and knowledge transfer to less-experienced team members.

  • Ability to collaborate effectively across cross-functional teams and support enterprise technology modernization initiatives.

Licenses and Certifications

None Required.

Physical Demands

The Physical Demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the Accountabilities and Essential Functions of the job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable an individual with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

This role will also support Accenture HSE Ventures and Acquisitions program, ensuring newly acquired companies are following HSE laws and company HSE requirements.   • Develop, execute and maintain the Global HSE Industrial Hygiene Program.
  • Ensure compliance with local HSE laws and regulations related to industrial hygiene.
  • Contribute to V&A HSE risk assessments and mitigation plans during Due Diligence and Post Merger Integration.
  • Assist in the creation and continuous improvement of Accenture HSE Policies and Procedures.
  • Participate in root cause analysis and corrective/preventative actions for occupational health/exposure incidents.
  • Ensure training needs are identified and developed for employees participating in industrial hygiene activities.
  • Embed artificial intelligence into industrial hygiene processes, where possible.
  • Contribute to global HSE tools, sites and dashboards including third-party verifiers like ISNetworld, Avetta, ComplyWorks, etc.
  • Provide input into the advancement of Accenture's HSE programs by sharing best practices and emerging knowledge, technology and innovation.
  • Engage with key stakeholders at the global and local levels within the organization to implement industrial hygiene processes and procedures to drive compliance and awareness.
  • Manage special projects for continual improvement.

Basic Qualifications

Minimum of 5 years Health & Safety and/or Environmental Science

Preferred Qualifications

  • Certified Industrial Hygienist and Certified Safety Professional (or international equivalent)
  • ISO 45001 & 14001 management system training.
  • Project Management certification (PMP Preferred)
  • Bachelor’s Degree in Occupational Health & Safety and/or Environmental Science and/or Industrial Hygiene, or related field
  • Knowledge and Experience with a variety of industry operations including but not limited to Oil & Gas, Data Centers, Nuclear, Manufacturing, Automation, Construction, Electrical, Maritime
  • Knowledge and certifications in Health & Safety (e.g. CSP, DOLE, CRSP, CSHM, IOSH Level 3, CHMM, NEBOSH IGC, etc.)
  • Knowledge and certifications in Industrial Hygiene (e.g. COH, CIH, DipOH, ROH, CPIH, etc.)
  • Mastery of the AIHA Strategy for Assessing and Managing Occupational Exposures
  • Knowledge of IH hazards and their relative controls such as chemical, physical, biological, and ergonomic stressors (including noise, radiation, thermal stressors, and ventilation.)

  • Experience with HSE and IH integration of Ventures and Acquisitions.
  • Ability to perform IH risk assessments of existing operations and acquired operations/facilities/site activities to identify gaps in local compliance regulations, company policies and procedures.

  • Excellent leadership, communication (written and oral) and interpersonal skills.

  • Fluent in English, both written and oral.
  • Ability to quickly grasp complex and unfamiliar subjects.
  • Ability to establish credibility as a member of the leadership team and with stakeholders.
  • Proven success in contributing to a virtual international team.
  • Highly responsive, flexible and adaptable.

Accenture Security is one of the fastest growing areas of our business, and our global Cyber Investigation and Forensic Response (CIFR) practice is at the heart of how we help clients prepare for, respond to, and recover from the most consequential cyber incidents. We deliver around-the-clock incident response services to our expanding portfolio of enterprise customers across the globe, providing expertise to multinational clients and shaping thought leadership inside and outside the firm.


You Are:

A hands-on technical leader who excels in complex investigations. You have deep expertise in Digital Forensics, Incident Response, and threat analysis, and you have the composure to apply it under pressure during active incidents. You are equally comfortable briefing clients in the boardroom and performing deep analysis. You take ownership of investigations, mentor the people around you, and you raise the bar on what world-class incident response looks like.


The Work:

  • Conduct complex forensic analysis including advanced memory forensics, malware triage, encrypted artifact recovery, and anti-forensics detection
  • Perform host and network digital forensics, log analysis, and threat hunting in support of incident response investigations
  • Leverage EDR solutions, cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, GCP), and threat intelligence to identify attacker Tactics, Techniques and Procedures (TTPs)
  • Conduct incident response within various Cloud, OT, and traditional enterprise environments
  • Develop indicators of compromise and contribute to comprehensive attack timelines
  • Create automation tools and scripts that improve team efficiency and investigation capabilities
  • Mentor and train 2-4 investigators across multiple cases, building team capability
  • Provide quality assurance on investigator findings before Primary Investigator review
  • Lead medium to large workstreams (20-50+ systems) with minimal oversight
  • Support Primary Investigators with technical decision-making and investigation strategy
  • Translate strategic investigation direction into tactical tasks for team execution
  • Effectively communicate and interface with customers, both technically and strategically, to customer stakeholders and legal counsel throughout the engagement lifecycle

We show you a phrase. Read it out loud and record it.

Steps

  1. Read the phrase shown on screen

Open worldwide: the task runs in 100+ countries. Remote, on your own schedule. Independent contractor, piecework; this is not an employment position.

jobs.excerpt: Position Summary The Datacenter Network Engineering (DNE) Air Traffic Control (ATC) Deployment Enablement Manager is the senior program leader accountable for converting approved DNE network designs and portfolio priorities into predictable execution across a data center fleet.
jobs.description:
Position Summary


The Datacenter Network Engineering (DNE) Air Traffic Control (ATC) Deployment Enablement Manager is the senior program leader accountable for converting approved DNE network designs and portfolio priorities into predictable execution across a data center fleet.

The role owns end-to-end delivery for front-end fabric infrastructure and assigned DNE programs, including new builds, technology modifications, retrofits, capacity expansions, and special projects. Accountability begins when scope is accepted for execution and continues through planning, material readiness, site execution, validation, operational handoff, and closeout.


This is a program leadership role first. The successful candidate will have enough technical fluency to understand data center fabric dependencies, challenge incomplete deployment packages, and lead informed conversations with engineers. The role does not configure network equipment or replace DNE's design authority. Its impact comes from creating clarity, sequencing complex work, aligning teams without direct authority, and delivering committed outcomes at fleet scale.


Why This Role Exists

DNE deployments span engineering, hardware supply, construction, logistics, site readiness, field execution, provisioning, and operations. Without a single execution owner, design changes, material constraints, and site dependencies can surface late and create avoidable schedule risk. The DNE ATC provides one accountable program lead who connects these systems and ensures that approved network capacity is delivered safely, consistently, and on time.


Primary Scope

  • Front-end data center fabric deployments
  • New data center network builds and expansions
  • Technology modifications and lifecycle retrofits
  • DNE hardware refreshes, migrations, and decommissions within the assigned portfolio
  • Special DNE projects that require cross-functional delivery coordination
  • Portfolio roadmapping, material readiness, and execution governance across multiple sites

Key Responsibilities

1. Portfolio Strategy and Roadmap Ownership

  • Build, own, and drive DNE's half-over-half execution roadmap across new builds, front-end fabric projects, technology modifications, retrofits, and special initiatives.
  • Translate approved Plan of Record and engineering priorities into an executable deployment portfolio with scope, milestones, sequencing, resource needs, and committed dates.
  • Evaluate new demand against portfolio capacity, hardware availability, site readiness, and existing commitments.
  • Lead prioritization and tradeoff discussions when multiple projects compete for shared hardware, engineering support, field resources, or deployment windows.
  • Maintain a single portfolio view of planned, committed, active, at-risk, and completed work.

2. Intake and Deployment Readiness

  • Own project intake and ensure each request has a clear business objective, scope, priority, target sites, schedule, accountable engineering owner, and acceptance criteria.
  • Validate that required execution artifacts are complete before commitment, including the Engineering Design Package (EDP), statement of work, Bill of Materials (BOM), Method of Procedure (MOP), deployment workflow, site-specific requirements, and dependency map.
  • Confirm that space, power, cabling, facilities, logistics, and site-access requirements are identified and owned.
  • Establish readiness gates and refuse false-start execution when critical scope, design, material, site, or ownership inputs are missing.
  • Document assumptions, exceptions, unresolved decisions, and the owner responsible for closing each gap.

3. End-to-End Deployment Delivery

  • Own program execution from accepted intake through kickoff, material delivery, field installation, provisioning, validation, operational handoff, and closeout.
  • Develop and maintain integrated schedules across DNE engineering, delivery engineering, Deployment, Design Engineering and Construction, site teams, logistics, sourcing, vendors, and operations.
  • Lead kickoff calls, weekly execution reviews, milestone checks, and decision forums with clear owners, due dates, and escalation paths.
  • Drive stage-gate completion and ensure downstream teams receive complete, timely, and actionable handoffs.
  • Verify that acceptance criteria, open defects, operational ownership, and residual risks are documented before closing a project.

4. Hardware Supply and Material Readiness

  • Own portfolio-level visibility into DNE hardware demand, supply, allocation, and deployment need-by dates.
  • Partner with logistics, sourcing, supply chain, and hardware program teams to validate BOMs, forecast demand, track purchase-order or pool allocation, and confirm material arrival at the Site Delivery Facility.
  • Identify shortages, substitutions, excess allocations, and late material before they affect committed milestones.
  • Lead allocation tradeoffs across projects and regions using documented priority, schedule impact, and business need.
  • Track emergency material requests and use recurring exceptions to improve BOM quality and intake readiness.

5. Risk, Dependency, and Change Management

  • Maintain a program risk and dependency register with quantified schedule impact, mitigation, owner, due date, and escalation threshold.
  • Identify cross-domain dependencies involving INE, Network AI, backbone, optical, facilities, construction, logistics, and site operations.
  • Own the programmatic change-control process for design updates, BOM changes, scope changes, priority changes, and schedule revisions.
  • Ensure approved changes are propagated to schedules, material plans, deployment workflows, trackers, and downstream teams.
  • Escalate strategically when a decision, resource constraint, or unresolved risk threatens scope, schedule, quality, or operational readiness.
  • Coordinate SEV-related program actions and ensure permanent follow-up work is tracked to closure.

6. Stakeholder Leadership and Executive Communication

  • Serve as the single point of program accountability for assigned DNE deployment portfolios.
  • Build productive partnerships across DNE design and delivery engineering, Deployment, procurement, sourcing, site teams, PM/PC partners, vendors, and operations.
  • Drive decisions and accountability without direct authority, using evidence, clear tradeoffs, and documented commitments.
  • Provide concise leadership updates that state where the portfolio stands, what is at risk, what has changed, and what decision or support is needed.
  • Present delivery health, capacity readiness, material risk, and execution trends in leadership and planning forums.

7. Tooling, Data Quality, and Reporting

  • Maintain accurate execution data.
  • Use deployment dashboards and hardware trackers to confirm physical-model and material dependencies where applicable.
  • Partner with engineering teams to understand workflow readiness and execution status.
  • Build automated status reporting, portfolio scorecards, dependency views, and exception-based reporting that reduce manual reconciliation.
  • Define data owners and resolve conflicting dates, statuses, or scope across systems before reporting program health.

8. Operational Excellence and Team Enablement

  • Lead retrospectives for significant deployments, delays, and repeat failure patterns.
  • Convert lessons learned into improved intake standards, readiness gates, templates, automation opportunities, and training.
  • Develop reusable playbooks for repeatable DNE deployment types.
  • Mentor PM/PC partners and new team members on DNE deployment processes, decision standards, and escalation practices.
  • Reduce duplicate meetings, manual reporting, and unclear handoffs while increasing visibility and accountability.

Required Skills and Qualifications

Program and Portfolio Leadership

  • 10+ years of technical program or portfolio management experience in network infrastructure, cloud infrastructure, data centers, telecommunications, or another large-scale physical infrastructure environment.
  • Demonstrated ownership of complex, multi-site deployment programs from intake through operational handoff.
  • Experience building roadmaps, integrated schedules, readiness gates, dependency models, risk registers, and measurable delivery commitments.
  • Proven ability to prioritize concurrent programs with shared hardware, engineering, and field resources.
  • Ability to drive decisions, accountability, and conflict resolution across teams without direct authority.
  • Strong executive communication skills, including concise written updates and confident leadership readouts.

DNE Technical Fluency

  • Working understanding of data center network fabrics, including front-end and backend boundaries, spine/leaf concepts, Top of Rack switching, fabric layers, physical topology, and redundancy.
  • Understanding of the deployment lifecycle: design, BOM, sourcing, staging, rack and stack, cabling, provisioning, quality assurance, acceptance, and operational handoff.
  • Ability to read and question an EDP, BOM, MOP, deployment workflow, dependency map, and site-readiness package.
  • Ability to discuss hardware, optics, cabling, power, space, and site dependencies with engineers without needing to perform the engineering work.
  • Experience operating in environments with evolving architectures, lifecycle retrofits, migrations, and first-of-a-kind deployment constraints.

Hardware and Supply Management

  • Experience with hardware demand planning, BOM management, material allocation, purchase-order or pool tracking, logistics, and supply-risk mitigation.
  • Ability to connect supply status to schedule confidence and make evidence-based allocation recommendations.

Data, Tools, and Process Improvement

  • Experience with project and engineering work-management tools.
  • Ability to build useful program metrics, dashboards, and automated reporting from imperfect operational data.
  • Demonstrated success simplifying workflows, eliminating manual toil, and improving execution through standardization or automation.
  • Strong attention to data quality, source-of-truth discipline, and decision traceability.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience delivering data center network fabric at hyperscale or across a large fleet.
  • Familiarity with DNE planning and deployment tools.
  • Experience with front-end fabric deployments, technology modifications, network lifecycle programs, hardware migrations, or decommissions.
  • Experience partnering with construction, facilities, supply chain, logistics, field engineering, vendors, and operations.
  • Experience with AI-assisted workflow optimization, automated reporting, or program analytics.
  • PMP, PgMP, network, cloud, or data center certification.

Education and Certifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Technology, Business, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • MBA or advanced degree is a plus.
  • PMP, PgMP, or equivalent program-management certification is preferred.
  • Network, cloud, or data center certifications are helpful but not required.

Additional Requirements

  • Must be US-based.
  • Ability to travel up to 15% for site visits, workshops, and deployment support.
  • Flexibility to support global deployments and stakeholders across time zones.

Salary Range

Where an applicant or employee is placed on this range will depend and be contingent on objective, documented work-related considerations like education, experience, certifications, licenses, preferred qualifications, among other factors.

jobs.title: Financial Controller:in (m/w/d)
jobs.excerpt: deine aufgaben Du liebst es, Zahlen und Kosten im Blick zu behalten, und willst Controlling neu denken, statt Reports von Hand zusammenzukopieren?
jobs.description:
deine aufgaben

Du liebst es, Zahlen und Kosten im Blick zu behalten, und willst Controlling neu denken, statt Reports von Hand zusammenzukopieren?

Als Financial Controller:in (m/w/d) bist du die zentrale Schnittstelle zwischen unseren operativen Abteilungen und der Geschäftsführung. Mit deinen Analysen und Reportings sorgst du für den nötigen Durchblick. Du überwachst die Profitabilität unserer Produkte, gestaltest unsere Businessplanung mit und professionalisierst unsere Prozesse. Dabei hilft dir KI, Routinearbeit zu automatisieren. So bleibt mehr Zeit für das, was zählt: die richtigen betriebswirtschaftlichen Schlüsse. Wenn du Lust hast, in einem jungen Team echte Verantwortung zu übernehmen, bist du hier genau richtig.

Deine Aufgaben

  • Operational Controlling: Du übernimmst das monatliche Reporting und analysierst unsere wichtigsten KPIs (u. a. ROAS, Contribution Margins, Logistikkosten) auf Herz und Nieren. Grundlage sind möglichst Daten aus unserem Data Warehouse statt manueller Exporte.

  • Businessplanung: Du unterstützt bei der Budgetplanung, u. a. für unsere Sales Events, und bei den rollierenden Forecasts. Dafür entwickelst du Planungsmodelle und Szenarien, die als fundierte Entscheidungsgrundlage für die Geschäftsführung dienen.

  • Soll-Ist-Vergleiche: Du erkennst Abweichungen zwischen Plan und Realität, suchst die Ursachen in den Daten und gibst konkrete Impulse für Gegenmaßnahmen.

  • Automatisierung & KI: Du nutzt KI-Tools (z. B. Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, Lovable) im Arbeitsalltag, um wiederkehrende Aufgaben zu automatisieren. Bei Bedarf baust du per Vibe Coding eigene Dashboards, Analyse-Tools oder kleine interne Anwendungen.

  • Datenqualität: Du verstehst unsere Datenflüsse (Shop, Marktplätze, Marketing, Buchhaltung) und erkennst Inkonsistenzen. Gemeinsam mit dem Data-Team arbeitest du an sauberen KPI-Definitionen und einer verlässlichen Datenbasis.

  • Schnittstellenmanagement: Du berätst unsere Abteilungen (z. B. Marketing, Einkauf & Logistik, Sales) in betriebswirtschaftlichen Fragen und unterstützt sie dabei, selbst mit Daten und KI Antworten zu finden.

dein profil

  • Studium: Du hast ein abgeschlossenes Studium der Betriebswirtschaftslehre mit Schwerpunkt Controlling/Finance oder eine vergleichbare Qualifikation.

  • Erfahrung: Du hast mindestens 2 Jahre Berufserfahrung im Controlling gesammelt, idealerweise im E-Commerce, Retail oder in einem dynamischen Start-up-Umfeld.

  • Fundierte BWL- und Finance-Kenntnisse: Du kennst dich sicher aus mit GuV, Deckungsbeitragsrechnung, Cashflow, Planung und Kennzahlenanalyse und weißt, was hinter den Zahlen steckt.

  • Analytisches Denken: Du erfasst komplexe Sachverhalte, erkennst Zusammenhänge und interpretierst Daten präzise.

  • Datenverständnis: Du verstehst, woher Zahlen kommen und wie sie zusammenhängen. Du erkennst, wenn etwas nicht plausibel ist, und hinterfragst Zahlen, bevor du sie präsentierst.

  • KI-Affinität: Du nutzt KI-Tools (z. B. ChatGPT, Claude) bereits aktiv im Arbeitsalltag und hast Lust, damit Prozesse zu verbessern. Erste Erfahrungen mit Vibe Coding sind ein Plus.

  • Teamfähigkeit & Hands-on-Mentalität: Du arbeitest gern im Team, bist neugierig und probierst neue Tools selbst aus.

warum wir?

Dich erwartet ein modernes und dynamisches Arbeitsumfeld mit einer Du-Kultur von Tag eins. Wir glauben an flache Hierarchien und agile Arbeitsmethoden. Unsere Teams bestehen aus motivierten Menschen, die etwas bewegen wollen.

  • Goodies für dich: Von Jobrad-Leasing über Zuschuss zum Deutschlandticket bis hin zu betrieblicher Altersvorsorge (Arbeitgeberzuschuss 50%) - bei uns profitierst du von vielen Extras. On top gibt’s Mitarbeitenden-Rabatt in unserem Snocks Coffee und einen steuerfreien Sachbezug (50€ / Monat), den du flexibel für deinen Wocheneinkauf oder z.B. eine Mitgliedschaft bei Urban Sports Club einsetzen kannst.
  • Arbeiten, wie’s zu dir passt: Du arbeitest, wo du am produktivsten bist. Remote ist Standard, aber wenn du doch mal Lust hast, ins Büro nach Mannheim, Hamburg oder Berlin zu kommen, gibt’s dafür ein Monatsbudget.
  • Echte Flexibilität: Ob Workation mit Freund:innen oder Kolleg:innen, morgendliches Yoga oder eine Sport-Session mittags – bei uns kannst du Arbeit und Privatleben easy miteinander verbinden.
  • Onboarding: Du startest nicht mit leeren Händen, sondern bekommst top Hardware, alles was du zum Arbeiten brauchst, und kannst dir im Welcome Shop coole Produkte von unseren Partnern & Friends aussuchen.
  • Du weißt nicht weiter? Wir unterstützen dich mit unseren Weiterbildungsangeboten und individuellen Development Budgets! Und wenns nicht ums Berufliche geht, kannst du deinen Zugang zur Gesundheitsplattform nilo.health nutzen, um dir den Support zu holen, den du brauchst.
  • Einfach (dir) mal was Gutes tun: Ob „Social Day“, um dich sozial zu engagieren, oder „Power Days“, wenn die Periode mal richtig zuschlägt – diese Tage gibt es on top zu deinem Urlaub.
  • Alle zusammen: Wir sind ein Team aus A-Playern, die nach Wachstum streben, und leben den Team-Spirit bei unseren grandiosen SNOCKS Group Events oder einfach beim nächsten After-Work.
  • Office-Leben: Bei uns wird’s nie langweilig: ob Tischtennis, Fifa oder Mario Kart nach der Arbeit, gemeinsames Kochen und Lunch, frisches Obst, Kaffee aus der Siebträgermaschine oder die Müsli-Bar. Und das Beste: Dein Haustier darf natürlich auch mit ins Office!
  • Wir kleiden dich ein: Noch keine Produkte der SNOCKS Group in deinem Kleiderschrank? Das ändern wir! Du erhältst jedes Jahr einen 360€ Gutschein von uns sowie weitere tolle Rabatte und Angebote wie bspw. Corporate Benefits.

Your customer-service experience can help nonprofit organizations advance meaningful causes.

We are seeking professional and compassionate individuals to answer inbound donor calls and accurately process donations and pledges for established nonprofit fundraising campaigns.

This is a remote1099 independent-contractor opportunityfor individuals who communicate clearly, follow procedures carefully, and understand the importance of treating every donor with professionalism and respect.

Donors Call You—No Solicitation Required

This opportunity involvesstrictly inbound donor calls.

There is:

  • No cold calling
  • No outbound dialing
  • No donor prospecting
  • No door-to-door or direct solicitation
  • No product selling

Donors voluntarily call after seeing, hearing, or responding to an existing nonprofit fundraising campaign. You will assist those callers by documenting their information and processing their intended donations or pledges.

Your Responsibilities

As a Nonprofit Donation Processor or Pledge Drive Specialist, you may:

  • Welcome and assist inbound donors
  • Follow campaign-approved scripts
  • Enter donation and pledge details accurately
  • Confirm important donor information
  • Answer appropriate process-related questions
  • Navigate multiple applications during calls
  • Protect confidential information
  • Follow compliance and quality requirements
  • Maintain dependable attendance during accepted servicing intervals

Requirements

Experience and Qualifications

Qualified applicants should have:

  • A high school diploma or GED
  • Six or more months of remote customer-service experience or at least one year of onsite experience
  • A professional and welcoming phone presence
  • Strong listening and verbal communication skills
  • Accurate typing and data-entry abilities
  • Comfort following scripts and structured processes
  • The ability to work without direct supervision
  • A dedicated, quiet home workspace

Required Technology

  • Windows 11 computer
  • Minimum 8GB RAM; 16GB recommended
  • Noise-canceling USB headset
  • Wired high-speed internet
  • Direct Ethernet connection
  • Quiet and distraction-free workspace

Dual monitors are recommended for ease of navigation.

MacBooks, Chromebooks, tablets, and Wi-Fi-only connections are not compatible.

Applicants should not purchase new equipment solely to submit an application. Equipment requirements should be confirmed before making a purchase.


Benefits

​

Contract Rate and Availability

  • Most campaigns offer approximately$13–$15 per hour
  • Rates and earning potential may vary by campaign and performance
  • Some campaigns provide servicing availability across a 24-hour operating schedule
  • Contractors choose from available servicing intervals
  • Consistent access depends on campaign demand and contractor performance

Before You Apply

Please understand:

  • This is an independent-contractor opportunity, not employment
  • Certification is required before servicing
  • Certification does not guarantee campaign placement
  • Available hours and campaigns may change
  • Contractors must honor the servicing intervals they select
  • Continued access depends on attendance, professionalism, quality, and performance

If you want to work from home while supporting organizations that depend on public generosity, this may be the right opportunity for you.

Apply today to be considered for a remote Nonprofit Donation Processor or Pledge Drive Specialist opportunity.

What you will do

Got a receipt that looks fake or edited? Photograph it, plus a real receipt from a similar shop, and point at what looks wrong.

Steps

  1. Photograph the receipt you think has been altered

  2. Photograph a genuine receipt from the same or a similar merchant

  3. Draw a box around the part that looks wrong

  • Do not alter a receipt yourself to create an example

jobs.description:
🏭Área: Ingeniería de Producto / Gestión de Configuración
⚙️Especialidad: PLM, eBOM e Integridad de Producto
👔Nivel: Especialista

¿Cuál será tu misión?

Garantizar la integridad, coherencia y trazabilidad de la información de producto a lo largo de todo su ciclo de vida. Gestionarás estructuras de producto, eBOM, configuraciones y datos maestros en entornos PLM y SAP, asegurando la correcta alineación entre Ingeniería, Compras, Producción, Calidad y otras áreas involucradas.

🔧Tus principales responsabilidades

  • Gestionar y mantener las estructuras de producto y listas de materiales de ingeniería (eBOM) en los sistemas PLM y SAP.

  • Garantizar la coherencia, calidad, integridad y trazabilidad de los datos de producto durante todo su ciclo de vida.

  • Coordinar la creación, modificación y liberación de artículos, documentos, componentes y estructuras de producto.

  • Analizar el impacto de cambios de diseño, revisiones y modificaciones de configuración sobre las estructuras de producto.

  • Gestionar procesos de Change Management, incluyendo solicitudes de cambio, órdenes de cambio, revisiones y estados de aprobación.

  • Verificar la correcta sincronización de la información entre las herramientas PLM, ERP/SAP y otros sistemas corporativos.

  • Identificar y resolver inconsistencias, duplicidades, errores de parametrización y problemas de calidad de datos.

  • Colaborar con Ingeniería de Producto en la definición y mantenimiento de configuraciones, variantes y opciones de producto.

  • Coordinarse con las áreas de Producción, Compras, Supply Chain, Calidad y Posventa para asegurar la correcta utilización de la información de producto.

  • Definir y aplicar criterios, procedimientos y estándares para la gestión de datos maestros y estructuras de producto.

  • Realizar controles, auditorías e informes de calidad de datos, integridad de estructuras y cumplimiento de procesos.

  • Participar en proyectos de mejora, migración, industrialización y optimización de sistemas PLM/SAP.

  • Documentar procesos, incidencias y soluciones, proporcionando soporte funcional a las personas usuarias.

👥El equipo

Trabajarás en coordinación con los equipos de Ingeniería, Gestión de Configuración, Industrialización, Producción, Compras, Calidad y Sistemas, actuando como persona de referencia para la integridad de la información de producto.

🎓¿Qué buscamos?

  • Titulación universitaria o formación técnica superior en Ingeniería Industrial, Organización Industrial, Informática, Gestión de Datos o áreas relacionadas.

  • Experiencia en gestión de datos de producto, estructuras de materiales, configuración de producto o procesos de ingeniería.

  • Experiencia trabajando con sistemas PLM y SAP, especialmente en la gestión de materiales, listas de materiales y cambios de ingeniería.

  • Conocimientos sólidos de estructuras eBOM, revisiones, versiones, configuraciones y trazabilidad de producto.

  • Conocimientos de procesos de Change Management y gestión del ciclo de vida del producto.

  • Se valorará experiencia con herramientas como Teamcenter, Windchill, ENOVIA, SAP PLM u otras soluciones equivalentes.

  • Conocimientos de integración entre sistemas PLM, ERP y herramientas de diseño o ingeniería.

  • Capacidad para analizar grandes volúmenes de información e identificar errores e inconsistencias de datos.

  • Dominio de Excel y experiencia con herramientas de análisis y reporting.

  • Se valorarán conocimientos de mBOM, procesos de industrialización, configuración de producto y gestión de datos maestros.

  • Persona organizada, rigurosa y orientada al detalle, con capacidad para trabajar de forma transversal.

  • Buenas habilidades de comunicación, coordinación y resolución de problemas.

  • Nivel de inglés B2 o superior, con capacidad para trabajar con documentación técnica y equipos internacionales.

🚀¿Qué ofrecemos?

  • Participación en proyectos de transformación y mejora de la gestión del ciclo de vida del producto.

  • Entorno técnico y multidisciplinar, con contacto directo con Ingeniería, Operaciones y Sistemas.

  • Oportunidades de desarrollo profesional en el ámbito de PLM, SAP, gestión de configuración y calidad de datos.

  • Proyecto estable y con posibilidades de crecimiento.

  • Modelo de trabajo y condiciones a concretar según la ubicación y las características del proyecto.

Position duration: ASAP to January 30, 2028

Location: Kenya, Madagascar, Mozambique, Ethiopia, South Sudan, Uganda, Zimbabwe, Malawi, Zambia

Note: this is the general coverage area of this role; this position is a Remote based position, and we will consider only qualified applicants located in these countries. Relocation is not available.

Project Overview 

Catholic Relief Services is implementing a global emergency response initiative designed to deliver timely, life‑saving humanitarian assistance in rapidly evolving crises worldwide. Over 18 months, the program enables fast, flexible action to address urgent needs arising from sudden shocks and protracted emergencies. It supports critical humanitarian sectors through context‑appropriate assistance while emphasizing operational readiness, locally led implementation, accountability to affected communities, and safe, dignified programming. Emergency Program Managers will support Kenya, Madagascar, Mozambique, Ethiopia, Sudan, South Sudan, Uganda, Zimbabwe, Malawi, and Zambia providing readiness and response support based on evolving needs, with the composition of countries adapted according to context and operational priorities. The initiative strengthens the organization’s ability to respond at speed and scale in complex and resource‑constrained environments, ensuring help reaches people most in need when it matters most.

Job Summary

You will manage and provide technical oversight of the development and implementation of the emergency response and recovery programming, particularly for large and complex projects, ensuring effective systems and processes are in place that support high-quality programming advancing Catholic Relief Services’ (CRS) work in serving the poor and vulnerable. The role contributes to CRS’ capacity, supporting target countries across a specified focus region, of emergency program across project cycle. Your management skills and knowledge will ensure that CRS delivers high-quality emergency programming and continuously works towards improving the impact of its emergency response and recovery programming.

The Emergency Program Manager I will work closely with program office, partners and other technical departments (WASH, Food Security, Cash, Shelter etc.) to support the establishment and strengthening program function, including hazard and risks mapping, response plan, MEAL readiness and donor communication channel. S/he will support the application of CRS program standards and donor requirements, contribute to readiness learning and support rapid response and lead readiness efforts for CRS program offices and partners to promote efficient, high quality and rapid humanitarian response.

Roles and Key Responsibilities

  • Provide management, guidance, and technical oversight of all new and existing emergency response and recovery projects throughout the project cycle to ensure project design, start-up, implementation and close-out are in line with CRS quality principles and standards, donor guidelines, and industry best practices.
  • Effectively manage talent for emergency response and recovery programs and supervise. Manage team dynamics and staff well-being. Provide coaching, strategically tailored individual development plans, and complete performance management for direct reports.
  • Oversee technical assistance and capacity strengthening activities in emergency response and recovery for staff and partner organizations to enhance program quality and impact.
  • Lead the development of program learning - identify opportunities for learning, research and publications in emergency response and recovery and implementation of MEAL policy. Facilitate the dissemination of promising practices and lessons learned to contribute to the agency's knowledge management agenda. Ensure integration of innovations and best practices.
  • Contribute to the proactive pursuit of opportunities for new funding to ensure growth of the program office (PO) emergency response and recovery portfolio in line with agency, regional, and PO strategic priorities. Serve as the technical lead and technical writer to ensure quality emergency response and recovery proposals per agency and donor standards. Contribute to budgeting and staffing plans and activities for proposals.
  • Oversee the identification, assessment and strengthening of partnerships relevant to emergency response and recovery and the appropriate application of partnership concepts, tools and approaches.
  • Ensure timely and appropriate project expenditures in line with financial plans and efficient use and stewardship of project material sources.
  • Represent CRS in relevant working groups and clusters, with key donors, and other local stakeholders.

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities

  • MEAL skills and experience.
  • Staff management experience and abilities that are conducive to a learning environment.
  • Experience using MS Windows and MS Office packages (Excel, Word, PowerPoint), Web Conferencing Applications, information management systems.
  • Good experience in project grants management, including project design, preferably for grants from multiple public donors, including US government and UN.
  • Demonstrated ability to write high quality technical proposals.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with ability to make sound judgment and decisions and offer innovative solutions.
  • Strong relations management abilities. Ability to relate to people at all levels internally and externally. Strategic in how you approach each relationship.
  • Good presentation and facilitation skills.
  • Proactive, resourceful, solutions-oriented and results-oriented.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Master's Degree in International Development, International Relations, Community Development, or in the field of WASH, shelter, livelihoods, or food security.
  • At least 1 year working experience in the area of emergency programming, including WASH, shelter, livelihoods, and/or food security programming.

Required Languages:Proficiency (verbal and written) in English is required; French and Portuguese is preferred.

Travel: Must be able and willing to travel at least 50% of time often at very short notice (within 48 hours) and for an average of four-six weeks (with a maximum of two consecutive months under exceptional circumstances). Should have the capacity to live and work in difficult/stressful environments and serve wherever agency needs dictate.
